verdict.rationale: Paddle documents a broad, unified Billing API with an OpenAPI 3.1 spec. Several areas are explicitly available through both the API and the dashboard: transactions, metrics, and reports. The official MCP server also exposes the full API, and dashboard workflows like pricing, billing, refunds and subscription changes can be handled by agents. However, nothing explicitly claims full UI–API parity, and some items appear dashboard-centric: API key creation is done under Paddle > Developer tools, and Retain payment-recovery configuration shows no API path. Missing for 10: an explicit parity guarantee, API coverage of key management and Retain/dunning configuration, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: We take care of payments, tax, subscriptions, and metrics with one unified API that does it all.
you can create your own transactions using the API or Paddle dashboard.
Filter, break down, and investigate the metrics and data available in your Paddle account from the dashboard or the API.
The Paddle Postman collection includes every operation, so you can try the API interactively before writing code.
Instead of navigating the dashboard or making API calls, you can ask an agent in natural language to handle pricing, billing, support, and integration workflows.
